extracted.intended_audience: attorneys, government contracting officers, judges, law students, and contractors dealing with U.S. federal government contracts
extracted.subtask_description: A digest of legal principles, statutory requirements, and adjudicated standards governing procurement and construction contracts with the United States (advertising, guaranties, assignments, damages, liabilities, bonds, labor claims, annulment, performance, etc.). Intended to guide legal analysis and contracting practice under U.S. federal law and Army regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where bidder dies within time limit, estate not bound
rubrics_metrics.description: Where bidder dies within time limit, estate not bound.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice called for in guaranty must be actual
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice called for in guaranty must be actual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constructive or mere publication may be insufficient where guaranty requires notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance after expiration of time limit not binding on guarantors
rubrics_metrics.description: Acceptance after expiration of time limit not binding on guarantors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blanket and general guaranties legal
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Blanket' and 'general' guaranties are legally effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulation requiring guaranties may be waived
rubrics_metrics.description: A regulation that requires guaranties may be waived under appropriate circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Omission to file guaranty not cured by filing bond after opening
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to file the required guaranty at the time specified is not cured by filing a bond after bid opening.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certified check may substantially comply with guaranty requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A certified check can constitute substantial compliance with a requirement for a guaranty in certain cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certified check: bidder not liable beyond amount
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a certified check is used in lieu of other guaranty, the bidder's liability is limited to the amount of the certified check.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where certified check was to be retained to secure contract, cash it and sue for balance
rubrics_metrics.description: If a certified check was intended to be retained to secure a contract, the government should cash it and then sue for any remaining loss beyond the check amount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical remedy guidance for recovery when certified check insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cash deposited to secure contract may be applied to complete work; balance returned
rubrics_metrics.description: Cash deposited to secure a contract can be applied to complete the work; any remaining balance should be returned to the contractor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advances of public money — rent may be paid in advance (sec. 3648 R.S.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under statutes addressing advances of public money, rent may be paid in advance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracts and expenditures in excess of appropriations — fiscal-year contracts (sec. 3679)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 3679 R.S. governs fiscal-year contracts and limits expenditures in excess of appropriations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes treatment of fiscal-year limitations and later amendments (e.g., March 3, 1905).

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory exceptions for subsistence and similar items (sec. 3732)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 3732 R.S. provides exceptions (e.g., subsistence) to general restrictions on contracts/expenditures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 3733 — buildings and public improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 3733 R.S. governs contracts for buildings and public improvements and their relation to appropriations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracts conditioned on future appropriations or imposing indefinite liability unauthorized
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracts conditioned upon future appropriations or that create indefinite liability for the United States are unauthorized and void.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment statutes (secs. 3477 and 3737) — general effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections 3477 and 3737 R.S. restrict assignments of government contracts; the digest explains their general effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment voidable not void
rubrics_metrics.description: An assignment in violation of the statutes may be voidable rather than absolutely void in some circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract provisions regarding assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties' contractual provisions regarding assignment are relevant and enforceable subject to statutory limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignments in bankruptcy, for benefit of creditors, etc., not included
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain assignments (e.g., by operation of insolvency law) may be treated differently and not be within the strict prohibitions of assignment statutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignments by operation of law — executors, etc., excluded
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignments by operation of law (executors, administrators) are generally not within prohibitions of assignment statutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Receiver bound and entitled to perform
rubrics_metrics.description: A receiver appointed for a contracting party may be bound by and entitled to perform the government contract under certain conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between assignment of contract and assignment of claim under contract
rubrics_metrics.description: Assigning the performance/benefit of a contract is distinct from assigning a post-contractual claim; different rules apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Money due under contract payable to contractor only
rubrics_metrics.description: Amounts due under a government contract are payable to the named contractor, not to third parties, absent lawful assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agreements with surety
rubrics_metrics.description: Agreements between contractor and surety can affect obligations and remedies; treated in relation to statutory and case law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instances of assignments void under section 3477
rubrics_metrics.description: Enumerated factual instances where assignments are void under section 3477 R.S.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purchases forbidden from persons in military service or with congressional interest (para. 603 Army Regs.1910)
rubrics_metrics.description: Paragraph 603 and related statutes/regulations forbid certain purchases from military personnel or where members of Congress have an interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paragraph 603 is directory only — officer under no statutory incapacity
rubrics_metrics.description: The prohibition in paragraph 603 may be considered directory rather than creating absolute statutory incapacity in some cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition does not apply where contract requires approval of Secretary of War
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a contract must be approved by the Secretary of War, the general prohibition (e.g., purchases from certain persons) may not apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition does not include civilian employees
rubrics_metrics.description: The restriction on purchases from persons in military service does not automatically include civilian employees unless statute/regulation so states.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition does not apply to wife of soldier carrying on independent business
rubrics_metrics.description: A soldier's wife engaged in an independent business may not be caught by the prohibition on purchases from military personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition does not apply where contract is with corporation in which officer holds stock
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracts with corporations in which an officer holds stock are not automatically forbidden by the cited regulation/statute in some contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracts involving members of Congress — sections 3739–3742 R.S.
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections 3739–3742 R.S. address contracts in which members of Congress have an interest; special rules apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lease of building by retired officer
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific treatment and precedents govern leases by retired officers to the government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracts to be in writing and signed at the end (sec. 3744) — scope and effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 3744 requires certain contracts to be in writing and signed at the end; the digest explains scope and effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance begun under accepted bid when contract not approved — bidder to be paid for work performed
rubrics_metrics.description: If performance begins under an accepted bid and the government refuses to approve the formal contract, the bidder may be entitled to payment for work performed.

rubrics_metrics.name: In absence of written contract no recovery for failure to perform
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally, absent the required written contract, recovery for breach may be barred under the statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of papers signed by one party only
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents signed by only one party to a required written contract may have limited effect under section 3744 and related law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracts for Soldiers' Home not within section 3744
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracts for the Soldiers' Home have been held not subject to the requirements of section 3744 in particular precedents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Army regulations (par. 558) as to methods of purchasing supplies
rubrics_metrics.description: Army Regulation paragraph 558 prescribes methods of purchasing supplies; treated in relation to statutory rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal written contract not required under Act of June 12, 1906 in some cases
rubrics_metrics.description: The Act of June 12, 1906 may obviate the need for a formal written contract in particular procurement situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficient signing under the statute
rubrics_metrics.description: What constitutes 'sufficient signing' under the statute is defined by case law and statutory interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Returns office — oaths — set-offs and right to withhold moneys due contractor
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules concerning returns offices, required oaths, set-offs, and the government's right to withhold payments to contractors are articulated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision for forfeiture may be a penalty
rubrics_metrics.description: A contractual provision providing for forfeiture can be characterized by courts as a penalty and may be unenforceable as such.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision for reduction in price may be a penalty
rubrics_metrics.description: A clause reducing price can operate as a penalty if it is disproportionate to actual damages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision for forfeiture of all retained percentages regarded as penalty
rubrics_metrics.description: Clauses forfeiting all retained percentages may be treated as penalties rather than liquidated damages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision for damages for failure as to any of two or more independent things may be a penalty
rubrics_metrics.description: Where damages are stipulated for failure on independent obligations, the aggregate may be treated as a penalty if excessive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forfeiture of certified check may be a penalty
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a certified check is forfeited as penalty, courts will examine whether the forfeiture is disproportionate to actual loss.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excessive stipulated damages will be regarded as penalty
rubrics_metrics.description: If stipulated damages are excessive compared to actual harm, they will be treated as penalties and not enforced as liquidated damages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delay by subcontractors no ground for relief to prime contractor
rubrics_metrics.description: Delay caused by subcontractors generally does not excuse or provide relief to the prime contractor absent contract terms allowing it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Damages where similar articles cannot be procured
rubrics_metrics.description: Where replacement of articles is required and similar articles cannot be procured, measure of damages may account for scarcity and increased costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal contractor liable for increased payments to other contractors for minor parts when his failure causes them
rubrics_metrics.description: A principal contractor is liable for additional payments the government must make to others for minor parts if caused by the principal's failure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Damages where delay amounts to abandonment of contract
rubrics_metrics.description: Where delay is so great it effectively abandons the contract, damages are measured accordingly and may permit termination/remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Damages where government abandons project and damages cannot be ascertained
rubrics_metrics.description: If the government abandons the project and damages cannot be ascertained, special rules apply to determine recoverable amounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contractor responsible for actual damages although none stipulated
rubrics_metrics.description: Even without stipulated damages, a contractor remains responsible for actual damages resulting from breach or nonperformance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where delay is chargeable to government
rubrics_metrics.description: If delay is attributable to the government, the contractor may be excused or entitled to relief/compensation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certified check given to secure return of plans — only actual damages can be deducted
rubrics_metrics.description: When a certified check is collateral to secure return of plans, only actual damages may be deducted from the check upon failure to return, not punitive sums.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laborers and material-men have no lien on Government property
rubrics_metrics.description: Laborers and material-men cannot assert a mechanic's or similar lien against government-owned property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior to act of Aug.13,1894 Secretary of War could not authorize subcontractor to sue on contractor's bond in name of U.S.
rubrics_metrics.description: Before the 1894 act, the Secretary of War lacked authority to permit a subcontractor to sue on the contractor's bond in the name of the United States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bonds under Act of Aug.13,1894 — scope and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Act of Aug.13,1894 defines scope of bonds, includes special rules (e.g., foreign-built vessels), and disallows certified checks in lieu of required bonds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit allegations required for application for copy of bond
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific allegations must be included in affidavits that accompany applications for copies of bonds under the statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: When copy of contract and bond should be furnished to subcontractors
rubrics_metrics.description: Subcontractors should be furnished copies of the contract and bond upon proper application under statutory guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: United States should not withhold money due contractor to pay contractor's debts or indemnify surety
rubrics_metrics.description: The government should not retain sums due a contractor to pay his private debts or to indemnify a surety absent legal authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double aspect of bond
rubrics_metrics.description: Bonds have a 'double aspect' protecting both the United States' interest and third-party claims; analysis depends on circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract between U.S. and municipality not within act
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracts between the United States and municipalities may fall outside certain statutes governing bonds and laborers' protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to pay subcontractors' claim not sufficient cause to strike surety from qualified list
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to pay subcontractor claims, by itself, may not justify removing a surety from the list of qualified sureties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignee in bankruptcy should give bond to protect labor and material-men
rubrics_metrics.description: An assignee in bankruptcy taking over contract obligations should give bond to protect laborers and material-men where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary contract with surety to finish work requires new bond
rubrics_metrics.description: If, upon default, a supplementary contract is made with the surety to finish the work, a new bond should be provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where work has been performed bond should be required before payment for protection of laborers/material-men
rubrics_metrics.description: If subcontractors/laborers have performed work, bond protections should be in place prior to payment to safeguard their claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copy furnished should be authenticated as required by section 882 R.S.
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of contract/bond furnished must be authenticated in conformity with section 882 R.S. when required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permission under Secretary of War not required to commence suit
rubrics_metrics.description: A claimant may commence suit without prior permission of the Secretary of War in some circumstances under the statutes/case law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annulment of contract by United States — positive action required where forfeiture follows
rubrics_metrics.description: Where annulment will lead to forfeiture, the government must take positive action indicating its intent to annul the contract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mere breach of a term insufficient to justify annulment
rubrics_metrics.description: A mere breach of contract term, standing alone, is insufficient to justify the government annulling the contract; substantial failure is needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annulment action final and cannot be rescinded
rubrics_metrics.description: An annulment of a contract by the government (when properly effected) is final and cannot later be rescinded by the same department in some contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract provisions permitting taking possession of contractor's plant on annulment — use on other improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a contract provides for possession/retention of a contractor's plant upon annulment, the government may use that plant for other improvements as provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: To justify annulment there must be substantial failure to perform faithfully
rubrics_metrics.description: Annulment is justified only where there is a substantial failure of the contractor to perform faithfully and materially.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unreasonable delay in commencing performance may be treated as abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: An unreasonable delay by a contractor in beginning performance may be treated by the government as abandonment of the contract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipatory breach — government need not await expiration before supplying deficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the contractor has anticipatorily breached, the government need not wait for the contractual time to run before taking steps to supply the deficiency and mitigate harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: No authority to restrict purchases to domestic production or forbid employment of aliens absent statute
rubrics_metrics.description: The executive has no general authority to limit purchases to domestic articles or forbid employment of aliens; such restrictions require statutory authorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: No authority to prevent use of convict labor absent statute; Executive Order May 18, 1905
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no general authority to prohibit convict labor unless authorized by statute; noted Executive Order (May 18, 1905) forbids employing persons undergoing sentences in certain contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aliens competent to bid for government work
rubrics_metrics.description: Aliens are competent to submit bids and contract for government work unless a statute provides otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract clause prohibiting convicts by subcontractors
rubrics_metrics.description: A contract term forbidding the contractor's suppliers/subcontractors from using convict labor is enforceable where included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for American material (Act of March 3, 1875)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Act of March 3, 1875 provides for preference to American-produced material in certain procurements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Act of March 4, 1917 regarding purchase of foreign material for fortifications
rubrics_metrics.description: The Act of March 4, 1917 addresses purchases of foreign material for fortifications and provides general authorization in defined circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract provision for increase or decrease in original quantity
rubrics_metrics.description: Contract clauses permitting increases or decreases in original quantities are proper and governed by contract terms and procurement rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Occupation of premises under contract imposes implied obligation not to injure them unnecessarily
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the government occupies premises under contract (express or implied) there is an implied duty to use the premises so as not to unnecessarily injure them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where description amounts to warranty
rubrics_metrics.description: If the contract description operates as a warranty of quality or condition, the contractor may be liable for breaches of that warranty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contractor responsible for loss by fire if fails to complete and government completes — may insure at contractor's expense
rubrics_metrics.description: If the contractor is responsible for loss by fire and fails to complete the building, and the government completes it, the government may insure the building at the contractor's expense under certain doctrines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where bidder fails to enter into contract contract may be made with guarantor as open-market transaction
rubrics_metrics.description: If the accepted bidder refuses to enter into contract, the government may proceed to contract with the guarantor or make an open-market purchase, depending on terms and statutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surety not entitled to perform absent provision to that effect
rubrics_metrics.description: A surety is not automatically entitled to perform the contract itself unless the bond or contract grants that right.

rubrics_metrics.name: After dissolution of partnership one member may be allowed to make contract
rubrics_metrics.description: Following dissolution of a partnership, one member may still be allowed to execute contracts in certain circumstances, subject to law and fact-specific rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payments may be made to any member of a partnership despite protests
rubrics_metrics.description: Payments to a member of a partnership may be valid even if another partner has filed a protest, depending on authority and facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Army regulations not strictly applicable to Soldiers' Home contracts should nonetheless be followed
rubrics_metrics.description: Even where Army regulations are not strictly applicable (e.g., Soldiers' Home), they should generally be followed as guidance in procurement practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract with employee to forfeit pay for quitting without notice is legal
rubrics_metrics.description: A contract clause requiring forfeiture of pay if an employee quits without notice has been held legal in certain precedents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soliciting bids for new fiscal year not an abandonment of government's renewal option
rubrics_metrics.description: Soliciting new bids for an upcoming fiscal year does not necessarily constitute an abandonment of the government's option to renew an existing contract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracts for printing for constructing quartermaster distinct from printing at department headquarters
rubrics_metrics.description: Procurement of printing for construction purposes may be treated differently than printing 'at department headquarters' under relevant regulations/case law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracts under War Department not required to be under seal
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the War Department practice and relevant law, certain contracts need not be under seal to be valid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approving officer may refuse to approve contract if bidder placed in hands of receiver
rubrics_metrics.description: If a bidder has been placed in receivership, the approving officer may refuse to approve the contract for reasons of financial responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approving officer may refuse to approve contract where articles bid are not suitable
rubrics_metrics.description: The approving officer may decline to approve an award where the articles bid are not considered suitable by the government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accidental fire not necessarily 'force or violence of the elements' — construction of 'by no fault of his own'
rubrics_metrics.description: An accidental fire may not be treated as 'force or violence of the elements' and courts closely construe language excusing liability 'by no fault of his own.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary services not required
rubrics_metrics.description: Where services are volunteered (not contracted), the government is not required to accept or compensate unless statute/contract provides.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional payment after completion to cover tariff duties may be made if contract terms allow
rubrics_metrics.description: Even after full completion, additional payment may be authorized under contract terms (e.g., to cover tariff duties paid) if the contract so provides.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract supplying forage for a particular station cannot be used to obtain forage beyond that station's needs
rubrics_metrics.description: A contract specifying supply to a particular station only cannot lawfully be used to obtain forage for other stations beyond the stated needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: 'Heirs, executors, and administrators' language not essential in contract
rubrics_metrics.description: Phrases like 'heirs, executors, and administrators' are not always essential to the validity or enforceability of a government contract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of 'locality' where hay called for of a certain grade of locality
rubrics_metrics.description: The statutory/contractual term 'locality' must be construed in context when hay or similar goods are specified by 'locality' and grade.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of provisions for dredging and excavating contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: Dredging and excavation contracts have specific construction rules and interpretations described in the digest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of post sewer benefiting water company — contracting to reduce price until savings equal sewer cost legal
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a government sewer benefits a water company from which the government purchases water, it may contract for a price reduction that accrues until the saving equals sewer cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delivery obligations commence from date of contract not from receipt of approved copy despite delay in approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if contract approval is delayed, delivery obligations should commence from the effective date of the contract rather than from receipt of an approved copy when instructions/bidders indicate otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stopping delivery after minimum quantity delivered constitutes election to order minimum quantity only
rubrics_metrics.description: If the government stops further deliveries after accepting the minimum ordered quantity, that action may constitute an election to order only the minimum quantity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paragraph 535 Army Regs. 1910 (assistance in preparation of proposals) applies to retired officers
rubrics_metrics.description: Army Regulation paragraph 535 regarding assistance in preparing proposals for contracts extends to retired officers in appropriate circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paragraph 663 Army Regs. 1910 forbids settlement with heirs, executors, etc.
rubrics_metrics.description: Paragraph 663 of Army Regulations 1910 addresses prohibitions on certain settlements with heirs and personal representatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 216 R.S. gives Secretary power to make regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 216 Revised Statutes vests the Secretary with authority to promulgate regulations relevant to procurement and contracts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 3651 R.S. as to making payments in money furnished to disbursing officer
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 3651 Revised Statutes governs payments properly made in money furnished to the disbursing officer; used in context of contracting/claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signing of vouchers, bonds, contracts, bids, etc., by typewriter or rubber stamp
rubrics_metrics.description: The use of a typewriter or rubber stamp to sign vouchers, bonds, contracts, bids etc. raises issues of sufficiency of signing under statute/case law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secretary of War may set aside his action on a contract any time before contractor has been notified
rubrics_metrics.description: The Secretary of War retains the power to set aside his approval of a contract at any time prior to notifying the contractor in some situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to render periodical reports does not prevent recovery for work omitted from report
rubrics_metrics.description: A contractor's failure to submit required periodic reports does not necessarily bar recovery for valid work performed but omitted from the reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partner has no authority to sign partnership instruments under seal absent authority
rubrics_metrics.description: A partner cannot bind the partnership by signing instruments 'under seal' unless the partnership or statute authorizes such execution by that partner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purchase not meeting strict government test may be accepted upon contractor giving bond to replace defective purchase
rubrics_metrics.description: If a purchase fails to meet strict government specifications, the purchase may still be accepted if the contractor gives a bond to replace it if found defective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stoppage of supplies (general doctrine)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules governing stoppage of supplies by contractors or the government are summarized and applied to procurement contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracting officer cannot designate officials before whom contract or bond shall be executed
rubrics_metrics.description: A contracting officer lacks authority to pre-designate the specific officials before whom a contract or bond must be executed in some statutory/regulatory contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transportation of troops or supplies through foreign country — legal/regulatory considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Special legal/regulatory considerations govern transportation of troops or supplies through foreign territory under government contracts and military necessities.

rubrics_metrics.name: U.S. cannot recover from government contractor damages resulting from proper blasting
rubrics_metrics.description: The United States cannot recover from its contractor for damages that result from blasting that was proper and performed according to contract/standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment to contractor where U.S. is in possession of plant alleged to infringe a patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Payment to a contractor may be proper even where the United States is in possession of plant constructed and the possession is alleged to infringe a patent; the digest cites controlling precedents and reasoning.
